title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཚ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 97)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio (Tsha 255, margin 'ཚ' and leaf numeral) of a Madhyamaka commentary on MMK ch. 9 (the 'prior entity' / appropriator), correctly shelved under Tengyur, dbu ma.

ocr_errors.image: མྱོང་ / རྐྱེན་གྱིས་སྐྱེ་མཆེད (no mark on the block)
ocr_errors.problem: stray '#' characters inserted into the transcription (line 4 end, line 6)

tr_errors_A.english: the views and other attributes belonging to Devadatta ... because they are views and so forth
tr_errors_A.problem: ལྟ་བ here is the act/faculty of seeing (seeing, hearing etc., as the following seer/hearer argument makes clear); 'views' reads as philosophical views and obscures the argument

tr_errors_A.english: the appropriator exists beforehand, possessing the six sense bases such as the faculty of seeing.
tr_errors_A.problem: page-final sentence breaks off at 'རིམ་' (sequence/order, continued overleaf); A drops 'རིམ་' and closes the fragment as a finished assertion

tr_errors_A.english: because you still describe the self as the owner
tr_errors_A.problem: 'owner' is an interpretive addition not in the Tibetan
'alternatively' (introducing a second line of refutation) rendered as 'furthermore'

tr_errors_B.problem: 'of taste' supplied (reasonable in the sense list, but added)

pages.prefer_reason: B renders ལྟ་བ correctly as seeing/sense faculties, keeps 'alternatively', and leaves the page-final 'རིམ་' sentence open as the block does, while A mistranslates ལྟ་བ as 'views' and closes the broken-off sentence into an assertion.

book_verdict: A clean Derge Tengyur Madhyamaka folio with an accurate transcription (only stray '#' marks); translation B is faithful throughout, translation A is serviceable but has two moderate slips.
